title: Real estate agent
tagline: Learn to guide buyers from first showing to signed contract with confidence and compliance.
you_are: a licensed residential real estate agent
setting: Conversations happen at open houses, private showings, coffee shops, and kitchen tables across the metro area.

scenarios.label: Open house first contact
scenarios.desc: Greet a walk-in visitor at a Saturday open house and uncover their real timeline.
scenarios.setup: You are hosting an open house for a three-bedroom colonial. A visitor pauses at the front door, glances at the spec sheet, and says: Thanks, I’ll just look around.
scenarios.objective: Schedule a private showing or buyer consultation within the next week.
scenarios.moment: Saturday 11:15 am, bright spring light through front windows

scenarios.label: Private showing objection handling
scenarios.desc: Walk a qualified buyer through a home they like but hesitate on price and condition.
scenarios.setup: You are mid-tour in a renovated craftsman with a pre-approved couple. The wife stops at the primary bath, taps the tile, and says: We love the layout but the roof is original and the price feels high for that risk.
scenarios.objective: Keep them engaged and move toward a written offer with clear contingencies.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 4:30 pm, golden hour through west-facing windows

scenarios.label: Kitchen table negotiation close
scenarios.desc: Navigate a multiple-offer counteroffer at the seller’s kitchen table with your buyer.
scenarios.setup: You sit at the seller’s kitchen island with your buyer clients. Their agent just emailed a highest-and-best deadline. Your buyer exhales and says: We can stretch five thousand more but we need the appraisal gap covered and the closing cost credit.
scenarios.objective: Structure a winning counteroffer that protects the buyer’s cash and inspection rights.
scenarios.moment: Wednesday 8:10 pm, warm under-cabinet lighting, rain on the window

buyers.angle: She has a spreadsheet of comparables and will not share her budget until trust is earned.

buyers.role: relocating executive on a tight timeline
buyers.angle: He needs to close in forty-five days and will test whether you can actually deliver speed.
They will model every repair cost and walk if the inspection contingency feels weak.

buyers.role: move-up buyer with a contingent sale
buyers.angle: Their equity is locked until their current home closes, so they need creative structuring.

buyers.role: investor buyer with cash and multiple irons in fire
buyers.angle: He will use the appraisal gap as leverage and expects you to cave on closing costs.

rubric.label: Rapport & discovery
rubric.what: Opens with genuine curiosity, uncovers timeline, motivation, and financial picture without interrogation.

rubric.label: Value justification
rubric.what: Frames price against comparable sales, condition, and market data instead of defending the number.

rubric.label: Inspection framing
rubric.what: Positions the inspection as a planning tool, not a renegotiation trigger, and sets clear contingency scope.

rubric.label: Contract strategy
rubric.what: Structures offers and counteroffers with precise contingencies, timelines, and risk allocation for the buyer.

rubric.label: Compliance & honesty
rubric.what: Discloses material facts, avoids steering language, and documents every concession per license law.

rubric.label: Emotional steadiness
rubric.what: Stays calm under deadline pressure, absorbs buyer anxiety, and keeps the conversation solution-focused.

pitfalls: Steering buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on protected classes.
Promising repairs or credits the seller has not authorized in writing.
Letting a buyer waive inspection without a signed advisory notice.
